The main events of this meeting on 20th July were the three miles Track Championship and the Hop, step and jump Championship. The first named resulted in a win for Jack Brown in 14mins. 32s. with P.

First home was Pat Newell, who took the lead on Cambridge Hill and thereafter drew steadily away to win by 13 seconds. Second was Pete Bagnall who used his speed to get past Eric Gebbett a mile from home.

Pete Bagnall was our first runner and handed over in third place having run quite well. Over stage 2 Charlie Smart was forced to drop back into 6th place, but after all we cannot expect miracles from a man of his age who, if the rest of the club were running up to standard would not be in the team.

Our first away fixture on 15th October was held at Addington and was a very satisfactory one for the Club. Pete Bagnall finished second, only four seconds behind the Herne Hill International, Mike Maynard.

Knight of Essex Beagles was the individual winner completing the course in record time and finishing in front of Sando. Pete Bagnall was our first man home in 11th position and supported by Masters, Short and L. Bishop, we gained 3rd place in the team event.
Pete Bagnall ran an excellent race to finish in fourth place, 80 seconds behind the winner, Maynard of Herne Hill. The remaining strength lay in the excellent packing of Jack Brown, P.
After being the leading Belgrave runner for a considerable distance, Peter Bagnall was passed in the last lap by Jack Brown who ran extremely well to finish 52nd.
Half way round the last lap it was noticed that even Pete Bagnall's stamina is not sufficient to run such a race on the small amount of training he has been able to manage.
